title: Verification flow — is the test-angle taxonomy live or decorative?

subject.mechanism: The test-angle taxonomy (criterion / reachability / seam / real_artifact / deployed, modifier must_block, conditional boundary / failure) and the machinery that is supposed to carry it end-to-end: AC store schema -> it-po authoring -> generate_ticket_from_ac.py -> ticket Test Requirements -> test-writer -> commit/CI gates -> deployed layout.
subject.failure_mode_guarded: 'Done does not mean done': code ships with a green AC-literal unit test but is never wired into anything that runs it. The taxonomy is the countermeasure — so the taxonomy itself becoming decorative is the highest-severity outcome, and this flow exists to make that detectable.
prior_incidents: A smoke gate blocked by a schema: user-surface-smoker routing was fully implemented in generate_ticket_from_ac.py (BP-1100f-5) while config/ac_store_schema.json had additionalProperties:false and no declares_side_effect property — so no AC could legally set the field that triggers it.
A live_dispatch enum in exactly one file: config/test_requirements.schema.json declares type: live_dispatch + surface_invoked, and nothing else in the repo reads them.

check_test_requirements_refs.py is named in test_requirements.schema.json's own description AND registered 'portable' in config/package_boundary.json, but the script does not exist anywhere in the repo.
A fast-lane runner that never executed its own gates (fast-lane-build.js, 2026-07-22; recorded in CLAUDE.md).
A done_proof hook that crashed in the deployed layout (ModuleNotFoundError: done_proof, missing from build_ac_store deploy_map; recorded in CLAUDE.md).

summary: A fully-green run of this flow would prove that a test angle is not merely a word in a document: that the AC store can hold the angle-triggering fields, that a real AC in the real store actually sets them, that the generator turns them into angle-tagged test descriptors and routes the side-effect gate agent, that test-writer's prompt carries the mandate, that a commit/CI gate BLOCKS an AC whose only coverage is the criterion angle, and that all of the above still holds in the built .leafcutter layout rather than only in the source tree. Today it is largely red: the vocabulary is expressible in one store and rejected by the other, the generator emits angles that no gate reads, zero of 2888 ACs set the field that arms the side-effect gate, and three enforcement agents sort AFTER commit so they cannot block anything.

core.criterion: The AC-literal happy path — the Then clause holds.
core.reachability: Invoke the REAL production entry point (subprocess/dispatch, not a direct import) and assert the behaviour happens AND its result is consumed in control flow.
core.seam: Feed real producer output into the real consumer and assert the CONSUMER's observable behaviour — no mocks on either side.
core.real_artifact: Use a fixture from the real serializer or a verbatim on-disk file; a fresh subprocess when the claim is about module load.
core.deployed: Run build.py to a temp target and exercise the DEPLOYED copy, not the source tree.

modifier.must_block: Marks a check whose SUBJECT is a gate/guard/validator: a paired negative-control test feeds known-bad input through the SAME entry point and must be shown to BLOCK. Most often it rides the `reachability` entry (that is where a gate's production entry point lives), but it attaches to whichever angle carries that entry point — in this flow it also rides `real_artifact` (VC-1.1/VC-1.2, where the gate IS a schema validator) and `seam` (VC-2.2, where the gate is the generator's routing branch). The modifier is about what is being guarded, not about which angle slot it occupies.

conditional.failure: Declared error path behaves as specified.

phases.name: The vocabulary is expressible
phases.intent: Prove the data model can physically HOLD angle information. Until a store accepts the field, every downstream consumer of that field is unreachable code by construction — this is the exact shape of the 'smoke gate blocked by a schema' incident.
phases.gate_rule: While any check here is red, no downstream phase can be trusted green: a green downstream check is testing a code path no real record can reach.
